summary:
Radar for 2026-10-22 (GLP-1 focus). Three things are moving right now:
(1) Retatrutide gray-market news has new, dated facts. CBS News bought and lab-tested vials sold as 'retatrutide' (published 21 Oct): one corner-store vial contained no peptide at all, plus bacteria. NSW Health reported 1,180 emergency department visits linked to unapproved peptides between July 2025 and September 2026, and 71% of them involved retatrutide. This is our strongest repeatable lane (Shorts median 103.5; retatrutide-named median 120) and the right material for a Lane B long-form.
(2) Two fresh named next-gen results qualify for Lane C. First, a CagriSema analysis in women: about 25% average weight loss versus 3% on placebo at 68 weeks, in about 2,300 women, presented at The Menopause Society and announced 20 Oct. It is right at the 48-hour edge, so ship it first. Second, retatrutide kidney data in obesity with chronic kidney disease (HCPLive, 22 Oct). The details still need checking against the primary source.
(3) A seasonal Lane A search opening: Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15–Dec 7, and local news is pushing '$50 a month GLP-1, who qualifies' (the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge). That is high-intent US search with almost no explainer competition from health channels.
The compounded tirzepatide recall is peaking. We already ran recall Shorts on 10-20 and 10-21, so the 1-recall-a-week rule and the 14-day long-form ban rule it out for now. Evergreen hooks refreshed this week: nausea (The Conversation, 22 Oct), hair loss (Yahoo, 22 Oct), GLP-1 'supplements' (Fortune, 22 Oct) and Halloween. I rejected a 'research-grade retatrutide sourcing checklist' article as unsafe. The 'MedPage incretin sleep apnea' headline couldn't be traced to a named drug or trial, so it's left out.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what CBS News' lab tests and NSW Health's emergency data confirm (Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form plus a 13:00 lead Short, in a calm 'What's Actually Confirmed?' frame. New dated facts: CBS News lab-tested vials sold as 'retatrutide' (21 Oct 2026); a corner-store vial had no peptide, just filler and 13 bacterial colonies. NSW Health recorded 1,180 ED presentations linked to unapproved peptides from July 2025 to September 2026, 71% involving retatrutide and about 18% leading to admission. The real retatrutide exists only in Lilly's trials and isn't approved anywhere. Close by pointing viewers to a prescriber about approved options or trial enrolment. Never name a seller, a price or how to buy.
candidates.why_now: CBS published the lab test on 21 Oct and syndication is still spreading (Yahoo, Newser). Australian NSW Health data landed 19–21 Oct, and the Penn/ScienceDaily AI-Reddit study is in the same feeds. Our retatrutide gray-market Shorts are our best performers (188, 120), and the CBS and NSW facts haven't been published by us yet.

evidence.signal: Bought and lab-tested vials sold as retatrutide; corner-store sample had no peptide, plus bacteria

evidence.source: The New Daily / NSW Health (19 Oct 2026)
evidence.signal: 1,180 ED presentations linked to unapproved peptides; 833 (71%) involved retatrutide
Picked up in mainstream science press 21–22 Oct
Two deaths reported to the FDA after products claiming to be retatrutide (context, previous snapshot)

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: about 25% average weight loss at 68 weeks, including by menopause stage (post hoc REDEFINE analysis, Menopause Society 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer with 'CagriSema' first in the title, e.g. 'CagriSema in Women: What the New Menopause Analysis Shows'. Key facts: about 2,300 women with obesity or overweight, about 25% versus 3% on placebo at 68 weeks. The menopause-stage split (26.7% premenopause, 24.8% perimenopause, 23.1% postmenopause) assumes everyone stayed on treatment, so say so. Call it a post hoc analysis, not a new trial, and note it isn't approved yet. Most users had stomach side effects, mostly mild to moderate. Run the funnel Short at 20:00 naming the long-form.
candidates.why_now: Announced 20 Oct and covered by CNBC, Reuters/Yahoo, Quartz and Pharmacy Times through 22 Oct. It's a fresh named next-gen result (the EloraTZP-type format, our only long-form above 50 views), and few health creators have covered the women-specific angle yet.

evidence.signal: 25% average weight loss in about 2,300 women versus 3% placebo at 68 weeks
Most users had digestive side effects
Post hoc analysis coverage still growing

candidates.topic: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge: who qualifies for $50-a-month Zepbound, Wegovy or Foundayo (open enrollment, Oct–Dec 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane A search question: 'Medicare GLP-1 $50 Program: Who Qualifies?' Explain the four eligibility requirements from the Medicare.gov fact sheet, which drugs are covered (Wegovy injection and tablets, Zepbound KwikPen, Foundayo), the dates (1 Jul 2026 to 31 Dec 2027), and that the $50 doesn't count toward the $2,100 Part D cap. Every line credited to Medicare.gov with a date, ending with 'ask your prescriber and plan'. No switching advice.
candidates.why_now: Medicare open enrollment (Oct 15–Dec 7) drives high-intent searches from older US adults, which means high ad rates. Local TV (WCPO, ABC7) ran '$50 a month, who qualifies' segments on 21–22 Oct. It's evergreen until the end of 2027.

evidence.signal: Official $50/month Bridge eligibility and covered drugs
'GLP-1 for $50 a month, here's who qualifies'
Explainer of the Bridge program

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and kidney disease: albuminuria and kidney pressure in adults with obesity and CKD (new data, HCPLive 22 Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer, 'Retatrutide and Kidneys: What the New CKD Data Show', but only after a scriptwriter confirms the primary source (likely the Phase 2 NCT05936151 kidney study): trial size, arms, timeframe and whether it was published or presented. Put it in context alongside semaglutide's FLOW trial in type 2 diabetes with CKD. Say clearly that retatrutide isn't approved and is only available in trials.
candidates.why_now: The HCPLive story went out 22 Oct (less than 48 h ago). Retatrutide is our top-performing drug name (Shorts median 120). It's a benefits-beyond-weight angle that hardly anyone has covered.

evidence.signal: 'Retatrutide Lowers Albuminuria, Glomerular Pressure in Obesity and CKD'
Phase 2 retatrutide kidney function study in overweight/obesity with CKD, completed
FLOW safety by CKD severity, for semaglutide context

candidates.topic: Hormone therapy plus semaglutide: linked to greater weight loss in menopausal women (real-world study)
candidates.angle: A body-effect Short that works on Instagram, run as the funnel for the CagriSema-in-women long-form. Women on menopause hormone therapy plus semaglutide lost more weight in a retrospective Mayo Clinic cohort (about 16% versus 12% at 12 months). Say 'linked to', not 'causes'; it's observational. Don't recommend starting hormone therapy; frame it as a question for your clinician.
candidates.why_now: Patient Care (22 Oct) and Medical News Today (21 Oct) are covering it in the same week as CagriSema's Menopause Society data and MedPage's 'GLP-1 in menopause'. A women-and-menopause cluster is forming across sources.

evidence.signal: 'Hormone therapy plus Wegovy linked to more weight loss'
Real-world study coverage
Semaglutide weight loss across pre-, peri- and postmenopause

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) side effects: which are common and what helps, with The Conversation's 22 Oct nausea piece and the Neurogastroenterol Motil review
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form: 'Tirzepatide Side Effects: Which Are Common and What Helps'. Cover how often nausea, diarrhoea and constipation happened in SURMOUNT-1 (people with obesity, no diabetes), the fact that they're mostly mild to moderate and ease over time, and label-backed eating tips. Use The Conversation's point that nausea is under-studied as the hook. Mark which warning signs mean calling your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: The Conversation (22 Oct) and Drugwatch's Mounjaro side-effects page (22 Oct) refresh a huge evergreen search. It's already planned in the playbook's Lane A list and has been seen in 2 snapshots.

evidence.signal: 'GLP-1 weight-loss drugs change how people eat, but nausea needs closer study'
Review of GLP-1 GI symptom events and motility

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 supplements' work like semaglutide or tirzepatide? What the evidence says (Fortune's 22 Oct 'GLP-1 boosters' guide)
candidates.angle: Myth-correction, Lane A: 'GLP-1 Supplements: Do They Work Like Ozempic?' Explain that the body's own GLP-1 lasts minutes while the medicines last about a week. Fibre, protein and eating order can nudge natural GLP-1, but no supplement has trial results like STEP or SURMOUNT. Positive tone, no product names, end with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Fortune's buying guide (22 Oct) plus a growing 'peptide economy' story show strong commercial search interest. It fits the 'natural ways to support your own GLP-1' pillar and gives a differentiated, evidence-first answer to an ad-driven query.

evidence.signal: 'The Best GLP-1 Boosters and Supplements (2026)'
Randomised crossover trial on chickpea structure and the small-intestine metabolome

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): how much of the weight lost is muscle? SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy, plus the 19 Oct semaglutide handgrip meta-analysis
candidates.angle: An 08:00 outcome-question Short ('How much is muscle?'). SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy: about three-quarters fat and about a quarter lean mass, which is similar to other diets. The handgrip meta-analysis adds 'strength mostly held up'. Then point to protein and strength training. Name the population (obesity without diabetes).
keywords: does ozempic make you lose muscle
candidates.why_now: Muscle outcome questions are proven for us (101, 131). The new handgrip meta-analysis (Diabetes Obes Metab, 19 Oct) adds a fact we haven't published. Seen in 3 snapshots.

evidence.signal: Meta-analysis of handgrip strength on semaglutide
Rapid review of protein and resistance training

candidates.topic: Hair loss on tirzepatide or semaglutide: why it happens and why it's usually temporary (Yahoo Health, 22 Oct)
candidates.angle: A single-drug body-effect Short. Hair shedding after rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium) shows up in trial side-effect tables at low rates, usually settles, and protein and adequate nutrition matter. Not a long-form: the hair-loss deep dive got 3. Reassuring, not scary.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health ran 'Yes, GLP-1 hair loss is real, but it doesn't last long' on 22 Oct. It's a high-volume search query and a body-effect angle that also fits Instagram.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 hair loss explainer

candidates.topic: Halloween candy on tirzepatide or semaglutide: why sweets may feel different ('food noise') and what helps
candidates.angle: A 'Life on GLP-1' Short for 28–31 Oct. GLP-1 acts on brain reward pathways, so many people report less 'food noise'. Large sugary portions can worsen nausea, so suggest smaller portions, eating slowly and staying hydrated. Positive, no diet policing. Can bridge into the Thanksgiving long-form in November.
keywords: can you eat sugar on ozempic
candidates.why_now: There's a fixed seasonal spike 9 days out, and the Thanksgiving guide (UC Davis) is already in 2 snapshots. Little GLP-1-specific Halloween content exists.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs change how people eat

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what's the difference? Oral semaglutide uptake is rising fast (Medical Xpress/HealthDay, 22 Oct)
candidates.angle: A two-drug-form head-to-head Short: oral semaglutide 25 mg (OASIS 4) versus 2.4 mg injection (STEP 1), clearly labelled as separate trials, not head-to-head. Cover how each is taken in general terms (no dosing) and common side effects. Include the line 'don't switch, stop or change your current medicines on your own'.
candidates.why_now: A new study shows rapid early uptake of oral semaglutide (22 Oct). Amazon Pharmacy now offers it, and Yahoo ran a doctor's comparison on 20 Oct. Search is growing. Use a Short only: the pill-vs-shot long-form got 9.

evidence.signal: Early uptake for oral semaglutide rapid relative to injectables
'Wegovy pill or Wegovy shot? A doctor explains'

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 and the STEP 1 extension, plus cost as a reason people stop
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form from the playbook list. Weight regain after stopping in the trials, what kept results going, and new real-world data on copay and price as the reason people stop (more than 1 million self-paying UK adults). It never tells anyone to stop; the message is 'plan with your prescriber'.
keywords: what happens when you stop ozempic
candidates.why_now: Steady demand, seen in 4 snapshots. The 2027 price cuts and Medicare Bridge news keep cost-driven stopping in the headlines.

evidence.signal: UK tirzepatide price-rise treatment patterns in more than 1 million self-payers
US semaglutide initiation behaviours, early stopping and 1-year persistence

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines for alcohol and addiction: what trials show, now that telehealth prescribes them off-label (STAT, 22 Oct)
candidates.angle: The 'promising early research' pillar. Cover the small RCTs of semaglutide in alcohol use disorder (reduced drinking measures) and the Addict Behav review, and stress that it isn't an approved use and larger trials are underway. Don't promote telehealth off-label access; say 'talk to a clinician about approved treatments'.
candidates.why_now: STAT (22 Oct) reports telehealth firms prescribing GLP-1s off-label for addiction, the BMJ covered a US trial on semaglutide and crime (20 Oct), and a new review is out (Oct 10).

evidence.signal: Telehealth off-label GLP-1 prescriptions for addiction
Review of semaglutide for alcohol use disorder
US trial testing semaglutide and criminality

candidates.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recall: what the FDA confirmed about the Apothecary Pharma vials (sterility, nationwide)
candidates.angle: Hold until 27 Oct or later. We ran recall Shorts on 10-20 and 10-21, so the 1-recall-a-week rule blocks a Short now, and the 14-day rule blocks a long-form. If there's a new dated FDA fact (expanded lots, a Class change), make a single 'what's confirmed' Short crediting the openFDA record. No #Mounjaro or #Zepbound.
candidates.why_now: USA Today, Fox Business, Good Housekeeping, the LA Times and BioPharma Dive are all on it (20–22 Oct). It's past its earliest stage and already covered by us.

evidence.signal: Compounded GLP-1 injections recalled nationwide
GLP-1 compounder issues recall for copycat Zepbound

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and depression: a new randomized trial on decision-making in major depressive disorder (Psychol Med, 21 Oct)
candidates.angle: An emerging-research Short for the mental-health thread. A small RCT looked at how people explore versus stick with choices, not depression cure rates. Be careful with scope: no claim that it treats depression, and include the line to talk to a clinician about mood changes.
candidates.why_now: A new RCT (21 Oct) adds to the Lancet Psychiatry cohort and News-Medical explainer already in 2 snapshots. Low competition, but emerging topics underperform for us.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide modulates explore/exploit decision-making in MDD, RCT

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'Retatrutide peptide: a quality-control checklist for sourcing research-grade material' (Pharmaceutical Technology, 22 Oct)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. It's a guide to sourcing an unapproved research chemical for injection, which breaks the 'never promote research-chemical sources' rule. Use the CBS and NSW 'what's confirmed' candidate instead.
candidates.why_now: Listed only so downstream agents don't pick it up from the feed.

evidence.signal: Sourcing checklist for 'research-grade' retatrutide
